transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been really stuck on how my face looks. The left side seems uneven and kind of puffy to me, especially on video calls or in photos from salsa, and people say they don’t notice it, but I can’t really stop thinking about it. It’s starting to affect work and… going out.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly to check, fix, or make sure your face looks right, like adjusting your hair, checking mirrors, or changing the way you hold your head?

Yeah… I do that. Mostly before meetings or if I’m going out. I’ll keep opening the camera preview and changing the angle or the lighting, and I mess with my hair to cover that side of my face.

Sometimes I retake pictures a lot, or I ask friends if I look… weird. It can take a while. I’ve been late because of it, or just too worn out to go.
Does the concern about your face ever make you feel extremely anxious, depressed, or cause problems in your relationships or at work?

Yeah… it has. Mostly work, I guess. I’ve missed some ticket deadlines, and I’ve joined video calls late because I couldn’t get past how I looked on camera. My supervisor brought it up in a performance review, which was… embarrassing.

And socially, I’ve skipped salsa nights and community events if I knew people would be taking photos.
How much time would you say you spend each day thinking about how your face looks, and does it feel hard to control those thoughts even when you try?

It’s… a lot of the day, honestly. I don’t know exactly, but it keeps coming back, especially if I’m on video or thinking about photos from salsa.

I try to tell myself people say they don’t see it, but I still get stuck on the left side looking uneven or puffy. It’s hard to just drop it.
Do you find yourself repeating certain behaviors or thoughts to try to reduce the anxiety or discomfort about how your face looks?

Yeah. I mean… I’ll keep checking the camera preview before meetings, changing the angle or lighting over and over. I fix my hair around that side of my face a lot.

If I’m going out, I’ll retake pictures or ask friends if I look strange. Sometimes I do it until I’m late, or just… too tired to go.
When you’re worried about how your face looks, is it mainly because you believe there’s a specific defect or flaw in your appearance that others might notice or judge?

Yeah… mostly that. I keep thinking the left side of my face looks uneven or kind of puffy, especially on video calls or in photos. Other people say they don’t notice anything, but I still feel like they might.
Are there times when you have unwanted or intrusive thoughts that aren’t about your appearance, or do your worries mostly focus on how you look?

Mostly it’s how I look. I mean, the thing I can’t seem to stop coming back to is the left side of my face looking uneven or puffy, especially on video calls or in salsa photos.

People tell me they don’t see it, but… it still feels like it’s there, and it’s been getting in the way with work and going out.

latest_inference.note: The patient's concerns are primarily focused on a perceived defect in appearance (asymmetry/puffiness of the left side of the face), repetitive checking and reassurance-seeking behaviors, and significant impairment in social and occupational functioning. These features align with body dysmorphic disorder (F45.22). Other candidates (F32.0, F40.10) are less consistent with the clinical picture as depression and social phobia alone do not fully account for the preoccupation with appearance and ritualistic behaviors described.
